title: Halting and correct output probability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, the sum over all time horizons of the probabilities that the run of $N$ has not halted is at most $T(|x|)$, and every run that halts outputs the one-symbol word indicating whether $x\in L$. Then, for every input $x$, every halting run outputs that correct one-symbol word, and a uniformly chosen Boolean choice word of length $2T(|x|)$ yields a halting run with that output with probability at least $1/2$.
